triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: And in the lodge there were only three servants: old Grigory, and his old wife Marfa, and a young man called Smerdyakov.

triples.subject: Marfa Ignatyevna
triples.quote: She was set on leaving Fyodor Pavlovitch and opening a little shop in Moscow with their small savings.

triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: They did not go away, and Fyodor Pavlovitch promised them a small sum for wages, and paid it regularly.

triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: It was impossible to tell at first sight whether he loved his meek, obedient wife; but he really did love her, and she knew it.

triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: I have mentioned already that Grigory had detested Adelaïda Ivanovna, the first wife of Fyodor Pavlovitch and the mother of Dmitri

triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: Grigory saw how his wife danced, and, an hour later, at home in their cottage he gave her a lesson, pulling her hair a little.

triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: When Adelaïda Ivanovna had run away, Grigory took Dmitri, then a child of three years old, combed his hair and washed him in a tub with his own hands, and looked after him for almost a year.

triples.subject: Grigory Vassilyevitch
triples.quote: Afterwards he had looked after Ivan and Alyosha, for which the general’s widow had rewarded him with a slap in the face; but I have already related all that.

triples.subject: Marfa
triples.quote: It happened that, on the very night after the burial of his child, Marfa was awakened by the wail of a new-born baby. She was frightened and waked her husband.

triples.subject: Grigory
triples.quote: Going back into the house, Grigory lighted a lantern, took the garden key, and taking no notice of the hysterical fears of his wife
